ops.title: APNs device registry: event sourcing, registration bounds, auto-prune
ops.body:
# APNs device registry: event sourcing, registration bounds, auto-prune

The direct APNs lane (`access/apns.go`, `access/apnsauth.go`) mirrors the Web Push sender's architecture (`access/push.go`, `access/vapid.go`) deliberately. These choices constrain future changes:

## Append-first event durability

Every registry write is append-then-project: the durable record is the event log under the well-known `push` subject (`push.device_register` / `push.device_unregister`, deduped by `DedupKey: "device:"+token`), and `apns_device_tokens` is only a projection. Never write the projection without the event; never invent a second source of truth. Prune order is likewise event-first, then `DELETE`.

## Registration bounds

- Body cap 1 KiB before decode (413 past it).
- Tokens must be even-length lowercase hex, 64–200 chars (Apple's tokens are 32 bytes today, but length is documented as variable).
- Stored set caps at 32 tokens (429 past it; re-registering a stored token always passes). The cap bounds the goroutines + outbound sockets each fan-out spawns per stored row — same rationale as `maxSubscriptions` in Web Push. Raise both together or neither.

## Auto-prune on unregistered devices

A 410 (Unregistered), or a 400 whose APNs reason is exactly `BadDeviceToken`, retires the token durably (unregister event + projection delete) and does *not* count as a fan-out failure. Any other non-2xx or transport error surfaces via `errors.Join` without pruning. Mirrors Web Push's 404/410 prune-on-gone.

## Transport and auth

- APNs requires HTTP/2: the real client is `&http.Client{Transport: &http2.Transport{}}` (x/net, h2-only). The `httpDoer` interface is the injected test boundary — keep the boundary at the HTTP client, not higher.
- Auth is a cached ES256 provider JWT (kid header, iss=TeamID, iat) minted from the referenced `.p8`; re-minted at 40 minutes, inside Apple's 20–60 minute acceptance window. The clock is injected (`APNSSender.now`) for the refresh-window tests.
- The pair bearer token never rides an APNs request or payload — only the provider token in the `Authorization` header. Push services sit outside the daemon's trust boundary.

## Lane enablement

Absent `apns.json` = disabled lane (zero `APNSConfig`, no sender constructed, no route mounted). A present-but-broken config or key fails loudly at daemon build — a configured lane never degrades silently.

## Known gap

Web Push subscriptions are purged by `ReconcileGrants` when the pair token rotates or remote access turns off; APNs device tokens have no equivalent reconciliation yet. If grant-surface revocation should cover APNs too, extend the reconcile pass rather than adding an ad-hoc purge.
ops.when: When modifying device token limits, adding pruning logic, changing the registration flow, or integrating additional push channels alongside APNs.
